Ford Had Another Name for the Mustang Dark Horse SC, Changed It Because It Was Weird
17 photos
Photo: Ford
Ford had a different name chosen for what we know today as the Mustang Dark Horse SC. The automaker had already filed trademarks for the designation in Europe and the United States. However, a last-minute decision sent the muscle car to the market with a different name than originally planned.
The original name choice for what we know as the Ford Mustang Dark Horse SC was Dark Horse Boss. Ford was ready to use it after filing trademarks for it long before the model went into production at the Flat Rock Assembly Plant in Flat Rock, Michigan, along with its Mustang siblings.
Instead, Ford moved forward into its new modern performance branding and chose the Mustang Dark Horse SC name, where the "SC" serves as a nod to the supercharged Predator V8 engine, roaring from under the hood. The choice aligns with Ford CEO Jim Farley’s naming strategy to avoid over-relying on nostalgic nameplates like the "Boss" or "Cobra," going instead in a forward-looking direction with the Mustang.
Ford also deliberately chose to drop the legendary Shelby nameplate for this GT500-level successor. Back in January, at the Detroit Motor Show, Jim Farley clarified that the car is built by the automaker’s own racing division.
Photo: Ford " This is a Ford Racing car, and the reality is that Shelby doesn't race. Our idea is for Ford Racing to actually develop road vehicles. They will develop our next-generation supercars, " he explained at the time. Furthermore, the Shelby brand no longer aligns with the customer demographic that Ford is after with muscle cars such as the Mustang Dark Horse SC.
Sources confirmed to Ford Authority that Ford's executives ultimately dropped the idea because combining the words created the phrase "Horse Boss." The team decided the combination sounded far too awkward for a performance vehicle and scrapped it.
The Dark Horse SC is the second-most powerful production Mustang ever built and the only one that is not light-years behind the almighty Mustang GTD and far above the non-SC Dark Horse. It comes with the 5.2-liter cross-plane crank Predator V8 with supercharged firepower.
While the non-SC version has to resort to 500 horsepower (507 metric horsepower) and 418 pound-feet (567 Newton meters) of torque, coming out of its Coyote 5.0-liter naturally aspirated V8, the Dark Horse SC boasts 795 horsepower (806 metric horsepower) and 660 pound-feet (895 Newton meters).
Photo: Ford Those are enough to make the Mustang Dark Horse SC rocket from zero to hero (0 to 60 mph or 0 to 97 kph) in just 2.9 seconds, run the quarter mile in 10.8 seconds with a trap speed of 131.8 mph, and max out at 180 mph (289 kph). For all these, customers pay a starting price of $106,585.

I Drove All of the Six New Cars in Gran Turismo 7 Around the Latest Circuit in the Game
26 photos
Photo: autoevolution
My neighbor from across the road just called me to ask if I could help his son fix their new PS5. It had an annoying account connection problem, and it took me 30 minutes to find a solution. Right after, I installed “My First Gran Turismo”, which is free to play.
We then set up his Logitech steering wheel, and I gave him some pointers before returning home for a session of Gran Turismo 7. With any luck, he should be fast enough in 12 months from now so we can race together online.
I was eager to dive into part one of the new Spec IV update, as I’ve been waiting for it for several weeks now. I went straight to Collector Level 90 after the update, which is the current maximum. I’m unsure about the Concierge section right now, and I’m definitely not a fan of how the Brand Experiences kicked off.
Instead of driving some Hyundai , Polestar, Xiaomi or Yangwang, I’d like easier access to some of the top-end Porsches, McLarens and Ferraris in the game.
Anyway, I’ll be back with more info on the latest changes soon, but for now I just wanted to drive all of the six new cars at Sugo. I don’t remember ever racing this track in any other video game before, but I’ve certainly seen plenty of real world videos of it.
Citroën 2 CV 6 Charleston '86 Photo: autoevolution I guess we all knew the Citroën 2 CV 6 Charleston would be the slowest car in this new update. There’s obviously a “cure” to that problem in the form of an engine swap which I haven’t explored yet. The flat-two, 602 cc engine in this thing is only good for 28 bhp.
At least the car weighs just slightly less than three Aprilia RS660 motorcycles, which is unheard of in 2026. I figured it would be the perfect machine to learn how to deal with the 13 corners at Sugo.
It’s running on Comfort Hard tires, and I almost couldn’t believe how fast it was losing (not gaining) speed going uphill towards the finish line. I barely made it up in third gear! I then found its limit going downhill, where it could go slightly faster than “advertised” (67 mph/109 kph).
Other than being slow, it made for a pleasant drive, but I could not convince myself to go for a second lap after the first one took me just over 150 seconds to complete.
Honda Step WGN Spada Premium Line '23 Photo: autoevolution I can think of a few Honda vehicles I would loved to see before the Step WGN Spada Premium Line '23, but I’m not the one in charge of this department.
After all, the Toyota Hiace Van DX '16 needed some competition, right? The turbocharged inline-four engine in the new minivan produces 147 bhp and 149.7lb-ft of torque, with the whole package weighing more than three times as much as the Citroen.
After the first few corners it simply felt like a sportscars in comparison to the old 2 CV, but then the uphill section revealed its true colors.
It wasn’t losing speed, but barely gaining it at just over 68 mph/110 kph. It didn’t manage to hit 100 mph (161 kph) going downhill, and it was still 30 seconds faster to the finish line versus the French machine.
Honda Civic Si Group A version '87 Photo: autoevolution Two Hondas in one update must feel like a special gift for fans of the Japanese brand. I’m still a VTEC guy at heart, as I’ve never really gotten over it even after switching to rotaries.
I’ve had mixed feelings about the Honda Civic Type R (EK) Touring Car before, as it felt strange to handle at times. And I wasn’t sure what to expect of he old Civic Si Group A.
The naturally-aspirated 1.6-liter engine produces a whopping 221 bhp, with roughly four times as many kgs (or roughly nine times as many pounds) to move around. I wasn’t sure if it was much faster than I expected, or if that feeling was just a consequence of driving it after the two slower cars.
I was stunned to see the speedometer at 105 mph/170+ kph going uphill. I kept going for three laps, and the fastest one was a 1:32.986. By the time I was done, I was already in love with both the Honda and Sugo. Still, the best was yet to come.
Ferrari F355 Berlinetta '94 Photo: autoevolution Let’s face it: the Ferrari F355 Berlinetta was the most highly-anticipated car for this update. We’re getting close to 30 of them right now, and I’m hopeful we’ll get there before GT8 arrives. With 374 bhp on tap, the F355 should be capable to top out at 186 mph (300 kph).
That won’t happen at Sugo though, as the main straight just isn’t long enough. I paid 360,000 credits for this car at the Used Car Dealership, which is almost three times as much as the Honda Civic cost in the Legends Car Dealership.
As the F355 is running on CS tires, I was skeptical it could be as fast as the Civic. Let’s just say there’s plenty of “dancing” involved if you plan to keep it going straight. With that kind of oversteer “problem”, it’s considerably more fun to drive than any of the previous vehicles on this list. You can close your eyes and still recognize it’s a Ferrari judging by the exhaust and engine note.
And it sent me into a nostalgia-hole as I reminisced of simpler, more peaceful times. It might be eight seconds slower to the finish line compared to the Civic, but I’m sure some basic mods can fix that.
MAZDA RX-VISION GT3 EVO '26 Photo: autoevolution Am I the only one who’s stuck in “wishful thinking” mode after Mazda’s latest 2030 Promise video? It opens up a long list of speculations if you want to go there, including the possibility that we’ll finally have an RX-7 successor in a few years.
Seeing the RX-Vision GT3 EVO ‘26 arriving in Gran Turismo 7 further fuels that hope in my mind, especially since we already had the MAZDA RX-VISION GT3 CONCEPT and the Mazda RX-VISION '15 in the game.
At first glance, the engine setup seems identical, with chassis and aero upgrades taking center stage. The new car will cost 150,000 credits more, though.
It was a familiar, but special experience to have it out at Sugo, and I’m sure 1:24.626 is by no means an accurate reflection of its true potential. Once I get up to 100 laps at this track, I’ll try for a sub 1:20 lap.
New Time Trial Photo: autoevolution When I signed in today, the new event had only been live for a few hours. The fastest driver in the world needed roughly 77.4 seconds for a complete lap of Sugo, with the target for gold sitting at around 79.7 seconds.
Anything that’s better than 1:24.500 should be good enough for Silver, but we’ll know for sure in a few days once the dust settles. The Xiaomi deal must be a fairly good one, otherwise I can’t explain why Polyphony would have us driving the Xiaomi Vision Gran Turismo around a Japanese track.
With 2,011 bhp on tap, we’re looking at an almost 1:1 power to weight ratio here (hp to kg). That means this VGT can go up to circa 243 mph (391 kph) but also that it needs an eternity to slow down in time for the next corner.
It costs one million credits at Brand Central and I didn’t buy it yet as I’m not sure I want to. My best lap was a 1:24.275 after two attempts, and I’d rather just explore what other Japanese cars can achieve at Sugo than go again. And yes, I’ll probably be stubborn about Chinese Evs for a very long time, although I’m tempted to say “forever”. I’ll be back with a report on the new Weekly Challenges soon!

Ford’s next electric pickup will start at around $30,000 when it goes on sale in early 2027. As its official debut draws closer, a disguised Fathom prototype popped up outside of Ford’s World Headquarters.
Ford Fathom EV pickup spotted, this time in Dearborn
Although we haven’t seen it in full yet, Ford’s Fathom is already making a name for itself. As the first model based on its new Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform, Ford promises the Fathom will be a step change from its previous-generation EVs.
Ford will open preorders for the Fathom in early 2027 with a starting MSRP of $28,350 for the standard-range version. With the $1,595 delivery fee, prices still start at under $30,000.
While that’s about half the cost of the F-150 Lightning, Ford’s first electric truck, the company says the price is the least interesting part.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
We got our first look at the Fathom in June after a prototype was captured driving around in Long Beach.
Last month, CEO Jim Farley revealed several images of camouflaged prototypes on the streets of Las Vegas in what appeared to be a photo shoot.
The latest image comes from Emily Gabler, Ford’s tech communication leader. Gabler posted an image of a covered Fathom outside of Ford’s World Headquarters in Dearborn, Michigan.
@Ford Fathom spotted on campus today in Dearborn. https://t.co/sD6hjspUpp — Emily Gabler (@chargedupemily) October 15, 2026
As we’ve seen in other images, the Fathom features a decent-sized sensor smack in the center up front to support driver-assist features.
Ford said the Fathom will be the first vehicle with Apple Maps directly integrated into the navigation system. All models will be BlueCruise-capable for hands-free driving. Other standard features include Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, plus bidirectional charging capabilities.
Ford Fathom EV pickup prototype (Source: Jim Farley)
We have yet to see it in full, but Ford said the interior features a “large touchscreen display,” with easy-to-use navigation using Apple Maps.
The midsize electric pickup will offer more interior space than a Toyota RAV4, and that’s not including the frunk (front trunk) or truck bed. Ford also said the Fathom will cost less to own over five years than a three-year-old used Tesla Model Y.
Ford midsize EV pickup spotted testing in Arizona (Source: KindelAuto)
By using lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries, Ford said it will reduce costs while preserving interior space.
While it has revealed a few details, Ford has yet to announce the battery size, driving range, and other key specs.
One thing we do know is that the Fathom will have an NACS port after a prototype was caught at a Tesla Supercharger over the summer.
Ford Fathom EV pickup spotted charging at a Tesla Supercharger (Source: Reddit)
Ford opened preorder invites this week for those who want to receive updates and to be among the first to own the new Fathom.
Preorders will officially open in early 2027, with the first customer deliveries expected to begin by the end of next year.
When asked if we will see the Fathom in full in 2026 or 2027, Gabler said, “Keep an eye out for early next year.”

The California-based defense company Kratos announced this week the first test flight of the uncrewed combat aircraft known as the U740 Valkyrie over European skies, as well as the first successful flight tests of a new turbojet engine designed for small aerial systems.
The U740 Valkyrie was developed through a partnership with the Dutch company Airbus in support of German and other European armed forces.
In a joint statement , Mike Schoellhorn, the chief executive of Airbus Defence and Space, explained that the Valkyrie combined Kratos’ low-cost airframe with Airbus’ sovereign European mission system.
“In an increasingly complex and contested threat environment, air forces require affordable combat mass today,” he said, adding that the Valkyrie will also support crewed combat aircraft with extended range, firepower and survivability.
The companies said the test flight accomplished all of their goals, including an independent rocket-assisted takeoff, maneuvers at various altitudes, speeds up to Mach 0.8, and in-flight mission adjustments.
According to the statement, the Valkyrie runs 30 feet in overall length with a 27-foot wingspan. It features an internal weapons bay for air-to-air and air-to-ground munitions. Additionally, it has a max take-off weight of more than 6,000 pounds, a range exceeding 3,000 miles and a service ceiling of 45,000 feet.
The companies added that the successful demonstration paves the way for more sophisticated test flights with Airbus’ Multi-platform Autonomous Reconfigurable and Secure mission system, or MARS.
They described MARS as the aircraft’s “European brain” because humans will still control all critical decisions despite the AI-enhanced software that allows the system to function autonomously.
Eric DeMarco, the president and CEO of Kratos, said that although “first flights typically include plenty of learning opportunities,” he called the test “an amazing success” because of the maturity of the technology.
The J85 Engine
This week, Kratos also announced recent flight tests of the TDI-J85 engine across multiple configurations, meaning it demonstrated capabilities for cruise missiles, decoys and unmanned aerial systems, or UAS.
“Our successful flight tests across diverse deployment methods prove the versatility and reliability of the TDI-J85 engine,” said Joseph Kovasity, a senior vice president of Kratos.
According to the statement , the J85 engine successfully launched from standard rail or zero-length launchers, an aircraft cargo bay and a launch container.
Kovasity added that Kratos recently scaled up operations because of manufacturing orders to build 3,000 engines in 2027, but the company is positioning itself to produce up to 10,000 engines or more per year by 2029.

Fleetworthy expanded its Expedited Inspection program to California, Michigan, Vermont and Maine on Tuesday, bringing the automated roadside inspection tool to five states. Nevada, the first, has used it since June 2025.
When a truck is selected for inspection, the program sends fleet and vehicle data and the driver’s electronic Record of Duty Status (eRODS) directly to the officer. Eligibility rests on two conditions: a fleet must use Fleetworthy’s Weigh Station Bypass service, which operated as Drivewyze before Bestpass-Fleetworthy Solutions bought it in 2024, and, for now, it must run ELDs from Geotab or Platform Science.
Fleetworthy called the Nevada launch the industry’s first automated roadside inspection solution and said enforcement officers there are already reporting time savings.
“With Expedited Inspection, we’re easily saving about 15 minutes per inspection. That’s time our officers get back to focus on enforcement, and time drivers get back on the road,” Sgt. Scott Keane of the Nevada Highway Patrol said in the release.
The company put a price on those minutes. Using the $91.27-per-hour marginal cost of operating a truck in the American Transportation Research Institute’s 2024 Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking , it estimates about $22.82 saved per inspection and said the impact can compound for fleets running frequent lanes through participating states.
How the data exchange works
Expedited Inspection handles the vehicle, fleet and hours-of-service information that drivers and officers trade at an inspection. The company describes it as Virtual Vehicle Enabled, a reference to Platform Science’s platform that pulls live data from trucks’ built-in telematics.
Emilie Campbell, vice president of marketplace for Virtual Vehicle at Platform Science, said the expansion “helps get accurate information into officers’ hands the moment it’s needed, without adding steps for drivers.”
The expansion also adds Inspect Queue, a view of every truck flagged for inspection that lets officers pick up an inspection on a separate device. It is live in all five states.
The program is free to state transportation departments and state police. It was developed with fleets, state agencies and enforcement partners, Fleetworthy said.
Availability
Expedited Inspection is available at no additional cost in Nevada, California, Michigan, Vermont and Maine for fleets using Weigh Station Bypass with a participating ELD provider. More states and ELD integrations are planned, Fleetworthy said.
“Expanding Expedited Inspection from one state to five shows how this technology can scale to reduce roadside friction for fleets and law enforcement,” said Miranda Leadbeater, a product manager at Fleetworthy. “Every minute saved means less downtime for drivers and more predictable operations for fleets.”

Honda's Tire Repair Kit Recall Is Back, Supplier Mistakenly Shipped Bad Replacements
12 photos
Photo: Honda
American Honda has filed a safety recall with the federal watchdog to repair a previous remedy. Known as 26V663 in the NHTSA's vernacular, the campaign is estimated to include 4,800-odd units of the CR-V Hybrid and Accord Hybrid in the United States of America, namely vehicles that were previously remedied under 26V366.
The previous campaign went public in June 2026, comprising a staggering 1,049,883 vehicles in the United States of America. Beyond the CR-V Hybrid and Accord Hybrid, the original safety recall also included the fuel-cell version of the RAV4 's biggest rival. Tire repair kits handed over as remedy were assembled around the same flawed parts the summer campaign was supposed to clear out.
American Honda's fix was to swap the kit's nozzle, and nothing more. But in the words of the automaker's recall filing, the supplier failed to separate old nozzles from the new ones. Troy, Michigan-based TEK Corporation is the supplier of both the suspect and the remedy kits.
As implied, the kit contains a nozzle that needs to be threaded onto the valve stem. The compressor is then switched on, allowing sealant to flow in to fix the puncture. Said nozzle carries a one-way valve that keeps everything moving toward the tire, not back into the kit's bottle. Connecting it wrong, pressure builds into the sealant bottle instead.
A relief valve does exist to bleed that off, but if it fails while the nozzle is seated wrong, the cap ultimately detaches. American Honda claims the cap can strike the user or anyone standing nearby, increasing the risk of injury. Not exactly the most pleasant experience, for sure, especially if you're kneeling on a highway shoulder at night with a flat tire.
Photo: Honda Per the automaker's report, American Honda counted zero injuries potentially related to the defect so far. 2,745 units of the CR-V Hybrid represent the biggest chunk of the affected population, with production dates ranging from September 8, 2022, through May 20, 2026.
The Accord Hybrid is listed with 2,058 units from January 6, 2023, to the same May 2026 cutoff. The collector's item is a single unit of the 2025 model year CR-V e:FCEV. Best described as a plug-in hydrogen fuel-cell electric crossover, the CR-V e:FCEV is exclusive to California.
A lease-only affair, the fuel-cell specification is exclusive to Calif because that's the only state with a proper hydrogen infrastructure for passenger vehicles. Hand-built in small batches in Marysville, Ohio, the CR-V e:FCEV packs two high-pressure hydrogen tanks and a 17.7-kWh traction battery. Said battery makes the design unusual, giving the CR-V e:FCEV Level 2 and Level 1 charging capability.
The subject unit was produced on December 9, 2024. The mix-up condition surfaced on July 3, 2026, when a Honda dealership reported the wrong countermeasure parts. A joint inventory dig with TEK followed, enabling America Honda to track down which vehicles may have received the wrong remedy tire repair kits.
Affected VINs will become searchable on the automaker's website and the NHTSA's recall portal on October 17, 2026. Dealer notifications have been sent, while customer notification letters should be mailed in November 2026.

Rivian’s point-to-point driving feature will first reach owners through an invitation-only “Autonomy Early Access Program,” and the owners it picks will have to sign a non-disclosure agreement to get in.
The program, laid out on a new Rivian support page , covers US R1 Gen 2 and R2 owners who pay for Autonomy+. Rivian says point-to-point launches to that group in late 2026 and won’t expand broadly until 2027.
Who gets in
Paying isn’t enough. Any Autonomy+ subscriber can raise their hand through an Autonomy Early Access tile in their Rivian account, but Rivian says invitations go to owners with an active paid subscription (trials don’t count), heavy use of its Autonomy features, and a clean recent safety record. It’ll also balance picks by region and vehicle model, starting in select states.
Gen 1 R1 owners are out. So are Canadians.

Rivian rechecks eligibility every 30 days and says membership is revocable at its discretion. Cancel Autonomy+, sell the vehicle, or fail one of those checks, and you lose access.
What testers sign up for
This is more work than a typical software beta. Participants have to use the preview features every week, log issues when it’s safe to do so, fill out monthly surveys, and be available for interviews or focus groups. They also have to enable data collection, including location and Camera Data Sharing.
And they have to keep quiet about it. Selected owners sign a Participation Agreement that includes an NDA covering program details, and the primary owner has to tell any secondary drivers that the vehicle is enrolled.
In return, testers get new Autonomy features early over the air, plus a newsletter. That’s the list. Rivian says participants aren’t paid.
Autonomy+ costs $2,500 one-time or $49.99 a month , and Rivian started charging for it in April after a free trial period. So the testers are paying customers doing unpaid product research for Rivian on top of their subscription.
The timeline keeps sliding
Point-to-point is the next big step for Rivian’s driver assistance. Universal Hands-Free, which Rivian rolled out with software update 2025.46 last December , lets drivers go hands-free on roads with painted lines, which Rivian puts at 3.5 million miles of roads in the US and Canada. But it won’t stop or slow down for traffic lights and stop signs. Point-to-point is supposed to handle the whole trip.
On Rivian’s Q2 earnings call in July, CEO RJ Scaringe described the first version as “Level 2++,” with hands off the wheel and eyes still on the road. He said hands-off, eyes-off driving comes in 2027, and Level 4 in 2028.
That’s a slip. In January 2025, Scaringe said Rivian would launch an “eyes-free” system in 2026 , and that attention-free highway driving would be available on the R2. Now eyes-off is a 2027 target, and the hands-off feature that was supposed to come before it is arriving in late 2026 as a limited, invite-only beta.
Rivian is also targeting the end of this year for its third-generation autonomy hardware, with its in-house RAP1 chip and lidar. We reported in May that Rivian was even considering building its own lidar . The early access program, though, runs on the R1 Gen 2 and R2 vehicles already on the road.
Rivian is taking a page from Tesla here. Tesla’s early “Full Self-Driving” Beta testers also signed NDAs, and Tesla later used its “Safety Score” to decide which paying owners got access, before eventually opening the beta to nearly everyone who bought the package.
Electrek’s Take
Picking drivers who actually use the system, who have a clean safety record, and rechecking them every month is the responsible way to put a beta driver assist feature on public roads. Tesla started out similarly and ended up handing FSD Beta to pretty much anyone who paid, and we’ve spent years covering what came after that.
As for timing, “late 2026” for a small group of invited owners in select states is a soft launch at best. Most R1 Gen 2 and R2 owners paying for Autonomy+ are looking at 2027, and eyes-off has already moved a year. Rivian has about 11 weeks to get point-to-point into anyone’s hands in 2026. U.S. Army Soldier assigned to the U.S. Army John F. Kennedy Special Warfare Center and School climbs an obstacle during an NFL-Army Special Operations Forces commercial production event at Camp Mackall, Hoffman, North Carolina, June 14, 2026. (U.S. Army photo by Spc. Roddie Arline)
WASHINGTON — As the US military reorganizes to rapidly deploy new drones and other unmanned weapons, the Army’s special operations school is building a cadre of exper t warrant officers to w rangle the robots on the battlefield: Military Occupational Specialty 390A , Robotics Technicians.
“If you really want to understand what a 390-Alpha is, what these warrant officers are capable of, I invite you out to Clarke Range , Alabama, during the first week in November,” said Maj. Gen. Jason Slider. That’s when the second-ever class of MOS 390A candidates will conduct their final field exercise. Inspired by lessons from battlefields in Ukraine , the Caucasus , and the Middle East , the wargame will stress-test the candidates’ capability to improvise under fi re, he explained.
“What we’re building is a soldier that can adapt a piece of robotic kit to the mission, to the enemy, to the terrain,” Slider said.
Slider commands the Army’s John F. Kennedy Special Warfare Center and School (SWCS), which graduated its first class of MOS 390A soldiers just two weeks ago . He and one of his chief aides, Chief Warrant Officer Michael Updike, spoke about the new program Tuesday at a GovExec event on the sidelines of the annual Association of the US Army conference .
As the simulated enemy presents a changing range of threats, the candidates will have to rethink their tactics and reprogram their robots on the fly, in the field, and under stress, Slider and Updike explained. Electronic warfare will scramble their radio control links, block GPS, and cut them off from cloud-based AI coding tools, forcing them to rely on only the technology they can bring with them and get to work in the mud.
“When everything goes black … they still have to be able to reach back into their toolkit and bring out those [programs] to put into the Raspberry Pi to get the robot to do what it needs to do,” Updike said. In the first class’s final exercise earlier this year, for example, the students fit a quadcopter with a $1,000 HD camera and connected it to a decentralized mesh network , enabling the data to route around jammed nodes.
“They have to do all that innovation in the field,” Updike emphasized, “without large models that are connected to the internet.”
Large Language Models, cloud-based services in general, and even GPS navigation are frequently jammed on battlefields in Ukraine. Even when they are available, soldiers must take care, lest their radio transmissions reveal their location to the enemy and bring down a devasting precision strike. The “final crucible” exercise at Clarke Range reflects that grueling modern battlefield.
“We had specifically designed this capstone exercise to drive failure,” Slider said. “[It] gives the students another opportunity to try — and maybe fail again.”
It’s crucial to understand what 390A soldiers are and what they aren’t, Slider emphasized. They’re not drone operators, although they can operate drones. They’re not programmers, although they can code, often using miniaturized AI tools small enough to run on a ruggedized laptop in the field. Instead, these warrant officers are technical experts who stand between the commissioned officers, who command the force, and the enlisted personnel, who specialize in operating specific systems.
The 390As act as “system integrators,” Updike explained, with both deep and broad understanding of different Army drones, ground robots, networks, and how they work together. Above all, the 390As are trained to adapt, modifying that array of interdependent systems to meet new threats.
“We looked at Nagorno-Karabakh and Ukraine, and we’re studying the ongoing conflicts in the Middle East,” Slider said. “We learned … units that that solely focus on pilots quickly lose the advantage to an adversary or an enemy force that can adapt.”
That adaptation can’t be solely technological, either, he said. It must encompass tactics and sheer human resilience as well.
“All the tech that we’re talking about is, I think, important, and it’ll help get the soldier to the objective,” Slider said. “But it’s always been true that the soldier has got to be really comfortable in the mud … closing with the enemy and finishing the fight.”

Posted By: Cecilia Jamasmie October 15, 2026
Cartier owner Richemont and U.S. jewellery retailer Signet Jewelers (NYSE: SIG) are discussing joining a consortium bidding for Anglo American’s (LSE: AAL) controlling stake in De Beers, Reuters and Bloomberg reported Thursday.
Anglo is selling its 85% holding in the diamond producer, with Botswana owning the rest. A potential deal has been reported at about $1 billion (C$1.43 billion), below De Beers’ $2.3-billion carrying value following three writedowns in as many years. The business recorded a $511-million underlying loss before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization on revenue of $3.5 billion last year, Anglo’s results show.
The prospective investors are discussing joining Global Diamond Consortium, led by former De Beers CEO Gareth Penny. Talks involving Richemont are advanced, although there’s no guarantee it will join, Bloomberg reported. The size of either company’s potential investment hasn’t been disclosed.
Their participation would bring major sellers of finished jewellery into the ownership of a struggling supplier of rough diamonds. De Beers has faced weaker Chinese demand and competition from lab-grown stones, while an investment would give the retailers greater influence over their natural-diamond supply chain. Signet and De Beers already launched a joint marketing campaign in 2024 to promote natural diamonds to younger U.S. couples.
Bidders
Global Diamond Consortium emerged as the preferred bidder in July, according to Botswana’s government. The group includes participation from the governments of Namibia and Angola and diamond manufacturers. It’s nearing an agreement that could increase Botswana’s holding to about 25%, Bloomberg reported Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter. Reuters said it couldn’t independently verify that report.
Botswana remains central to any transaction because it holds a right of first refusal and hasn’t said whether it will exercise it. The country supplied about 70% of De Beers’ rough-diamond production last year. A presidency spokesperson said Tuesday the government wouldn’t comment until a transaction had been concluded and signed, Reuters reported. Officials said this summer they expected completion in the fourth quarter.
Richemont, controlled by South African billionaire Johann Rupert, owns Cartier, Van Cleef & Arpels and watchmaker Vacheron Constantin. Signet’s brands include Kay, Zales, Jared and Canada’s Peoples Jewellers. Investment by jewellery interests in mining isn’t unprecedented: Graff Investments holds 15% of Gem Diamonds (LSE: GEMD), which operates Lesotho’s Letšeng mine.
Anglo put De Beers up for sale in May 2024 as part of a broader restructuring after fending off BHP’s (ASX: BHP) takeover approach. Independent diamond analyst Paul Zimnisky told MINING.COM earlier this year that a buyer with sufficient capital and strong execution could revive the business, with the loss of competing independent producers and sanctions on Russian diamonds strengthening its longer-term supply position.

Penske Automotive Group (NYSE: PAG) , a publicly-traded company that includes the current Penske-related companies involved in a closely-watched liability case , will become a private company with a buyout from two of its current corporate owners.
After a review of the July offer from Penske Corp and Mitsui & Co. Ltd ., PAG said Thursday it had accepted the offer to sell itself to those two companies. What is being sold is the approximately 27.8% of Penske Automotive those two companies do not currently own.
After the deal is completed, Penske Corp., which is a private company, will own 64% of Penske Automotive. Mitsui will own the balance.
The purchase price is $212 per share. When the offer to take PAG private was first announced in July, the share price in the deal was $210 per share.
That price, according to the prepared statement released by Penske Automotive, is a premium of approximately 20.09% to the 60-day average and 26.17% to the 90-day volume average weighted prices of PAG stock for the period ended July 21, when the offer was made.
According to the company’s 10-K report to the Securities & Exchange Commission, Penske Automotive, whose key activity is automotive retail, had revenue in 2025 of approximately $27.5 billion from retail automotive dealerships, $3.4 billion from retail commercial truck dealers, and $922.6 million from commercial vehicle distribution and other operations.
Its truck dealership operates as Premier Truck Group, which primarily sells Freightliner and Western Star trucks, both manufactured by Daimler Truck (DTG.DE) .
Penske Automotive holds a 28.9% share in Penske Truck Leasing. In the 10-K, the company said Penske Transportation Solutions (PTS) is the “universal brand name for Penske Truck Leasing’s various businesses, which articulates the breadth of their services.”
“PTS is capable of meeting customers’ needs across the supply chain with a broad product offering that includes full-service truck leasing, truck rental, and contract maintenance along with logistics services, such as dedicated contract carriage, distribution center management, supply chain management, and dry van truckload carrier services,” the 10-K said.
It is carrier Penske Logistics and its brokerage affiliate, Penske Transportation Management (PTM), which are part of PTS, that find themselves in a case involving carrier liability that has drawn strong interest across the industry.
The chain of events in the case is that Penske Logistics secured a load of automotive seats, which it then brokered out to its affiliate PTM.
PTM then brokered the load to another carrier who in turn brokered the freight to yet another carrier. That carrier was involved in the fatal 2018 crash.
After a lower court victory that found Penske was not liable, the Penske companies were defeated on appeal by the Fifth Circuit, which ruled Penske Logistics, several steps away from the carrier that killed Lyndon Dean Meyer on the day after Christmas, could be held liable for that fatal crash.
Penske Logistics is asking the full circuit for an en banc hearing to reconsider the appellate court decision in the Fifth Circuit.

2027 BMW F 450 RR Is the New Kid on the Block and I Didn’t See It Coming
44 photos
Photo: BMW Motorrad
My wife’s cousin used to be a biker when he was in college. His life has started moving at a much slower pace when he became a dad eight years ago, though. We still talk about motorcycles when we meet, and I can tell he’s still itching to get back on two wheels soon.
He must have read my recent “Ridden” review , as he wrote to ask for some advice on buying a new bike. I wasn’t ready for what followed. “It’s not for me, it’s for my daughter.” I didn’t even know she wanted one, but apparently she’ll be going to the dirt track with her new electric ride on Saturday.
Start’em young, right? I always say that step by step progression is crucial in this world. I’ve seen far too many young riders who were quick to jump on a 600 cc, supersport machine, only to end up in the hospital soon after the purchase. The European rule book didn’t stop them from claiming they had limited their rides, even though achieving the target figures was often times impossible.
While that category of bikes seems to have faded away, many manufacturers have started paying more attention to the middle-weight sector, in between 600 to 800 ccs. But closing the gap from A1-compliant (11 KW tops/15 HP) to A2-compliant (35 KW/48 HP) machines asked for an even more category-specific product in the 400 to 500 cc region.
In the past, BMW has had the G 310 R in that category, and I raced one for a few weekends at the track back in 2020. The single-cylinder setup wasn’t something you’d expect from a sporty BMW motorcycle though, and it felt too far-removed from the S 1000 RR which is easily one of the most revered bikes money can buy today.
When the German manufacture introduced the F 450 GS last year, I didn’t think about it too much. It wasn’t until I rode the company’s F 900 GSA earlier this year that I realized how much I might liked to have its “smaller” sibling when I was still a novice.
Somehow I didn’t realize this model was part of a broader strategy, which is why I was almost shocked seeing the F 450 RR today. It looks like a baby S 1000 RR , which should be great for sales. And I’m sure it has more to offer than that. The 420 cc engine has a maximum output of 48 hp at 8,750 rpm, and 31.7 lb-ft (43 Nm) of torque at 6,750.
Eighty percent of the torque is available at 3,000 rpm, which means you don’t have to constantly rev this thing to the redline to enjoy riding it. The RR weighs just as much as the GS (178 kg), which means it’s just slightly heavier than the Aprilia RS 457 (6.6 lbs/3 kg). The 14-liter fuel tank should be good enough for a maximum range of 217 miles/350 km, and you get plenty of goodies for a package that could easily cost less than $10,000.
I have mixed feelings about the front section of the bike right now, but will withhold any conclusions until I see it in the real world. There’s a lot of information to take in, and I’ll be sure to come up with a longer story analyzing more of the specs and comparing the F 450 RR to its competitors.

"Every Old Car Has Rust": Owner Sells 1958 Chevrolet Impala Parked for Too Many Years
9 photos
Photo: Facebook Marketplace
Every old car has rust. This is how the owner begins the description of this Impala, trying to justify the obvious corrosion you’ll find on the car.
This 1958 Impala has been sitting for God knows how long, so it’s now a project that needs complete restoration. That’s why it’s here in the first place. It needs to convince someone online to take it home, begin a complete restoration, and bring it back to the road.
The owner doesn’t share many specifics, so my recommendation from the get-go is to call them and ask all your questions. A walkaround video is a good place to start, but if you’re interested in an Impala that can be parked in your collection, an in-person inspection is necessary.
Photo: Facebook Marketplace The 1958 model year is without a doubt the most collectible Impala ever released. It was the first Impala, with Chevrolet needing just two years to bring this nameplate from the drawing board to the production channel.
Presented in 1956 as a concept at GM’s motor show, the Impala graduated to a production model in 1958. It was part of the Bel Air lineup and could be had as a convertible or as a hardtop.
The Impala was a successful release from the very first days on the market. It immediately generated impressive excitement, eventually propelling Chevrolet to the leading spot in the American car space. The GM brand ended the year with over 1.25 million cars sold to local buyers, whereas Ford , the company which until that point dominated the domestic automotive industry, fell to second place with 1.03 million cars.
The Impala was not an affordable car. The hardtop started at $2,586, while the base convertible carried a price tag of $2,724.
The Impala was offered with a wide range of engines, as Chevrolet wanted the new car to appeal to as many buyers as possible. The base choice was a 235 six rated at 145 horsepower, while the 283, which debuted only a year earlier, represented the entry in the V8 series. The 283 was offered in multiple more powerful choices, including with 270 horsepower if buyers were willing to pay $183 more.
The 348 was the big news of the year, as it represented the big-block option full-size Chevy buyers were waiting for. The 348 also joined the lineup with several configurations, including the highly-desirable Special Turbo-Thrust Tr-Power with 315 horsepower.
Photo: Facebook Marketplace This Impala landed on Facebook Marketplace without much information. Unfortunately, reading the door plate is quite difficult, considering its current condition, so it’s impossible to tell what engine is hiding under the hood - if an engine is still there, in the first place.
The seller claims that most of the parts are still there, so it’s probably safe to assume that an engine is also available. I wouldn’t expect this Impala to be fitted with a 348, as this would have been a major selling point, and not mentioning it in the listing would be quite a mistake.
Otherwise, this Impala is by all means a restoration project. It suffers from obvious rust damage, and the seller says this is no different from other old cars. I don’t think this is true, as many old cars that have been babied and stored inside are now spotless, even without a previous restoration.
Photo: Facebook Marketplace This Impala has been parked for many years, and this explains its current condition. That’s why I recommended that you request a walkaround video or go there in person, as assuming that this Impala can be restored to day-one specifications is impossible without additional details.
I can’t help but insist on the obvious part: this is a 1958 Impala, and these cars are becoming rarer. Keeping them original should be a priority, especially if the right engine is under the hood. Not everybody likes a six, but a 1958 Impala that still has the factory-installed 235 is a fantastic car, even if it’s not worth as much as a 348-powered sibling.
The six was a good choice for someone who wanted to drive the Impala daily, and I would always choose a 235 over a non-original engine.
Photo: Facebook Marketplace As for the price of this Impala, I can’t say I’m surprised, but I think the owner should have offered more information about the car and what you can find under the hood. They want $13,500 for this Impala, so give them a call and see what this mysterious hardtop is all about.
If you don’t live very far from Jurupa Valley, California, paying the owner a visit is probably the right thing to do if you’re committed to a purchase. It’s unclear if the Impala can move on its own, so for the time being, you should also consider shipping costs, especially if the vehicle must go on a long trip to reach your garage.

Manitoba’s brownfields PL gold mine, which Minnova plans to bring back online by 2028. Credit: Minnova
Posted By: Henry Lazenby October 15, 2026
Minnova (TSXV: MCI; US-OTC: AGRDF) outlined a $53.4-million (C$76.2-million) plan to bring Manitoba’s PL gold mine back into production in 2028, using existing infrastructure to limit upfront spending.
The operation near Sherridon, roughly 630 km northwest of Winnipeg, would average 62,200 oz. annually over 10 years, according to a preliminary economic assessment (PEA) released Wednesday.
“This PEA confirms what we have believed about the PL gold mine: a high-grade open pit start, an existing mill and infrastructure and a modest capital requirement combine to deliver a short payback and strong returns,” President and CEO Gorden Glenn said in the release.
Starting with surface ore could help Minnova generate cash before relying entirely on underground mining. The approach recasts an earlier development plan that centred on underground production, giving the company a longer operating horizon to support its restart ambitions.
High grade
PL’s September resource estimate contains 3.76 million measured and indicated tonnes grading 4.98 grams gold per tonne for 601,158 ounces. Another 1.67 million inferred tonnes grade 3.78 grams for 202,810 ounces.
The open-pit portion includes 1.58 million measured and indicated tonnes grading 5.28 grams, containing 268,091 ounces. Lower reporting cut-off grades and changed mining constraints prevent a direct comparison with the historical resource estimate, Minnova says.
Minnova shares fell 3.2% to C15¢ by midday Thursday in Toronto, valuing the company at about C$19 million ($13 million). They’ve traded between 14¢ and 50¢ over the past year.
Cost exposure
At $3,000-per-oz. gold, the new assessment projects a $180.6-million after-tax net present value, discounted at 5%, and a 111% internal rate of return. Payback would take about eight months from production.
All-in sustaining costs are estimated at $2,288 per oz. A 20% gold-price decline to $2,400 cuts the after-tax value to $5 million. The open pits require moving about 21 tonnes of waste for every tonne of ore.
The company’s 2017 feasibility study envisaged a five-year operation producing about 46,500 oz. annually, mostly from underground mining. It estimated all-in sustaining costs of $942 per ounce.
That earlier study assumed gold at $1,250 per oz. and excluded inferred resources from its production plan. Different study standards, mining plans and price assumptions mean its returns aren’t directly comparable with the new assessment.
Minnova had already set out plans last month to expand its existing 1,000-tonne-per-day plant to 2,000 tonnes in the second operating year. That would allow higher output while surface mining supplies the mill, before the operation shifts underground.
Resource expansion
The update followed more than 13,500 metres of drilling in 131 holes between September last year and April, targeting resource expansion and improving confidence in the deposit, the company said in July.
The site, formerly known as Puffy Lake, operated from December 1987 to March 1989 before mining stopped, according to an environmental assessment filed with Manitoba.
Minnova plans further resource updates, metallurgical testing and work toward a prefeasibility study. Its existing environmental licence covers underground mining. The company’s development plans also call for amendments to accommodate open pits and new underground access.

On Aug. 21, 2026, the Army announced the award of a prototype Other Transaction Agreement to the Georgia Tech Research Institute, Atlanta, Georgia, to serve as the Weapon Systems Integrator. (U.S. Army National Guard photo by Sgt. Grayson Cavaliere)
WASHINGTON — The Army is looking to expand its Common Autonomous Multi-Domain Launcher (CAML) program by adding a third, light variant in partnership with the Australian military.
“I’ve been asked by the vice [chief of staff] and our acting chief to execute in conjunction with the Australians a CAML-light sprint to help the Australians meet some of their capability requirements,” Lt. Gen. Frank Lozano, the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Fires, told an audience at the annual AUSA conference Wednesday.
He added that a request for information (RFI) will be coming out in the near future, and the service is looking to make some “early selections” in the March to April timeframe that could result in a a “potential” live-fire demo in either June or July , later leading to a down select.
Lozano did not disclose details on why the Army is looking for a light variant — the Army has previously stated it was looking for just medium and heavy variants — nor did he share details on the Australian military’s role in the program.
The CAML program is set to serve as a replacement for the Army’s Typhon — its Mid-Range Capability (MRC) long-range launcher — after the service discovered it was too large to operate on the battlefield. The new launchers will be an autonomous, optionally crewed, “highly mobile” cross-domain fires launcher designed to be air transportable.
The announcement of the light variant comes after the service awarded Georgia Tech Research Institute in September up to $33.4 million to be the lead weapons systems integrator for the medium variant of CAML. Lozano said Wednesday that a munitions palette provider and the autonomous platform provider for the medium program should be awarded in the next 30 days.
As for the heavy variant, Lozano said Wednesday that his office is “starting to look” at the 2028-2029 timeframe for the launcher.
“We’re looking at a strategy here where we take a scenario where we don’t have every missile having its own unique launcher and [we’re] trying to collapse down [to] a maximum of three,” Lozano said. “But that generically is the timeline, and we massage and adjust that timeline as we learn more about industry’s capabilities to deliver what we need.”
Similar to the medium CAML variant, Lozano emphasized that there will be more than one vendor working on the light variant to avoid “m anufacturing constraint” on the defense industrial base. “We have to break the old tradition of doing a competition and going down to one vendor, and then going all in on one single vendor, because then you just created a sole source environment, a choke point, and a manufacturing constraint,” Lozano said. “The intent is we want to be able to have multiple different missile and munition solutions for every type of capability requirement we’re trying to develop.”

This Gorgeous Aussie Tiny Home Is All About Warmth, Comfort, and Indoor-Outdoor Living
20 photos
Photo: LJM Tiny Homes
Sometimes, too much focus on minimalism and simplicity in tiny home design can result in living spaces that feel cold and sterile. Clean lines, neutral colors, and uncluttered spaces are all well and good, but a home needs warmth and personality to feel inviting.
Designers can keep a tiny home simple and clutter-free without making it feel dull by using natural wood grains, layered materials, and soft textiles, and ditching harsh overhead lights in favor of warm mood lighting. The Cooloola tiny house does all that and achieves the right balance between minimalism and liveliness.
This beautiful home on wheels is one of the latest creations from Australian builder LJM Tiny Homes and transforms minimalist design into a form of art by integrating warm wood tones, curved furniture, hidden and layered ambient lighting, and generous openings to the outdoors. It combines a contemporary exterior with an open-plan living area, a generous U-shaped kitchen, and two sleeping lofts, providing a highly livable dwelling for a couple or even a small family.
From the outside, the Cooloola has all the attributes of a genuine Australian tiny home . It features white Colorbond steel cladding and ample glazing, which combine with a skillion roofline, black window frames, and a wooden deck to give the home a contemporary appearance.
Photo: LJM Tiny Homes What makes this model truly stand out is the way it connects indoor and outdoor living. One glance through the large tri-fold entry door is enough to spot the gorgeous living area that opens up completely to the front deck. Next to it, a wide bistro-style window acts as a pass-through bar from the kitchen, creating a serving counter where you can enjoy breakfast, coffee, or a casual drink in the open air.
Apart from adding bar stools under that large servery window, owners can also put patio furniture on the spacious wooden deck, transforming it into an integrated outdoor living area, perfect for evenings with friends. With such an arrangement, the deck would feel like a natural extension of the kitchen and living room.
The abundance of glazing creates an open feel inside as well, while also pulling in views of the surrounding natural landscape. The team at LJM Tiny Homes created a warm aesthetic and welcoming ambiance by using woods of different shades, soft textiles, and beautiful decor. Light-colored plywood panels cover the walls and ceilings, while also accentuating the darker walnut-toned cabinetry that adds depth and richness to the living space.
Photo: LJM Tiny Homes The central living area is the kind of space that invites relaxation with a book in hand. It is furnished with a beautiful L-shaped sofa with rounded edges, white cushions, and subtle lighting under the seating, making it look like it’s floating. The sofa is paired with a modern round coffee table and faces the large folding door for beautiful views.
Another distinctive feature of this welcoming lounge is a custom-built dark wood shelving unit with an arched top section, which provides display space for books, framed photos, and decorative items. Lighting also plays an important role in creating a more inviting atmosphere than in other tiny houses . During the day, light pours in not only through the main door but also through a skylight just above the lounge, and at night, indirect lighting and accent lamps help create a soft, candle-like glow.
The massive U-shaped kitchen that wraps around one end of the ground floor is a chef’s dream. The wraparound countertops provide plenty of workspace for food preparation, and the layout keeps the cooking zone distinct from the living area without completely separating it.
Photo: LJM Tiny Homes One section of the countertop doubles as a breakfast bar, which combines with the large servery window to enhance the seamless indoor-outdoor flow. This setup makes the kitchen quite versatile, making it suitable for everything from cooking everyday meals to relaxed outdoor entertaining.
The wood-toned cabinetry is paired with a stainless steel countertop that adds a tinge of industrial vibe to the culinary space, and there are no upper cabinets to obstruct the views. In terms of functionality, the kitchen is equipped with a gas range and oven, a full-sized refrigerator, a dishwasher, a sink, and a pull-out pantry.
A narrow hallway leads from the living area to the bathroom and the stairs to one of the sleeping lofts. The bathroom is quite spacious for a tiny house and includes a full shower with a glass door and a window to the outside, a stylish suspended sink, and a composting toilet. Storage is integrated behind the toilet, while a large cabinet covers the opposite wall.
Photo: LJM Tiny Homes For sleeping, the Cooloola has two lofts positioned at either end of the house. Both are typical tiny house lofts with limited headroom, but are quite cozy and accommodate queen-size mattresses. While the loft above the bathroom is reached via the storage-integrated staircase, the one above the kitchen is accessed by a simple wooden ladder.
At 8.4 meters (27.5 feet) long, 2.5 meters (8.2 feet) wide, and 4.3 meters (14.1 feet) tall, this home is Rover-compliant (the Australian Road Standards), which makes it an appealing option for those who want to travel or change location frequently.
It sits on a custom-built, tri-axle flatbed steel trailer with adjustable leg supports, electric brakes on all six wheels, and a breakaway system, and structurally, it is built with Truecore steel framing, including the internal walls, with an insulated composite subfloor and insulated walls and ceiling.
With its warm aesthetic, practical features, and indoor-outdoor living setup, the Cooloola proves tiny homes can be a pleasure to live in. Price-wise, this model starts from AUD $83,600, which is about USD $57,850 at current exchange rates.

Tomplan Does Toy Hauler Campers Differently – Composite Midi Cargo XL Weighs As Little as 772 Lbs
15 photos
Photo: Micro Camper
Heading out into virgin ground and not knowing what you’ll find while exploring the wilderness is quite attractive, with the downside being that you can only cover so much ground in the couple days you’re out there. So, the industry spat out the toy hauler, and today, we explore a rather special and unique option.
It’s called the Midi Cargo XL, and while it may look like an AT-ST (Chicken Walker) out of Star Wars and even stores little humans inside, it serves a completely opposite purpose other than intergalactic warfare; this one’s all about the leisure side of life and designed to carry some of our toys to unexplored corners of our planet. But there are some catches to the story, and that’s what we’re here to find out.
Photo: Micro Camper First and foremost, we need to consider what sort of trailer we’re working with here, and using the word toy hauler, even though that’s what it is, may have you thinking about tossing an ATV inside, and while there is room for one in terms of cargo-carrying capacity, the lack of large rear door and ramp limits what sort of cargo we can stuff inside.
This leaves us with things like kayaks, e-bikes, fishing and climbing gear, and outdoor tents and dining sets. There are 400 kg (882 lbs) of cargo wiggle room for your gear and standard, or in its Basic layout, the Cargo XL weighs around 350 kg (772 lbs) and has a GVWR of 750 kg (1,653 lbs).
While it may not sound like much, there is a reason why Tomplan Trailers, the hearts and hands behind the design limit the GVWR : in Europe, it allows vehicle owners to tow without any special driver’s license classes, as long as the vehicle and trailer together roll in under 3,500 kg.
Photo: Tomplan More on the storage side of things, there is an outdoor hatch that allows us to stuff gear under the bed, and more under-bed storage is granted by a drawer, accessible from inside. Do take note that the basic Cargo XL is a completely empty shell, and includes no bed, drawers, creature comforts, heater, or any other camping features. The Full model is the one with goodies inside.
With all the camper features inside, or the Full model, the Cargo XL weighs around an extra 100 kg (220 lbs), leaving us with 300 kg (662 lbs) to work with, plenty for a couple of e-bikes, and other essentials.
How is such a low weight possible? By how the Cargo XL is built. At its core, Tomplan used an all- composite makeup with a foam core for its shell, providing thermal insulation and rigidity while keeping things light. The Full does include an electric heater inside to keep things comfortable outside of summer temperatures.
Photo: Tomplan Other features we find inside which make up the Full version include a fridge, the furniture we see lining the upper level of the camper, and 230 V and 12 V sockets and electrical, and the sink with faucet. Only a portable toilet can be brought along on our outings, so we’ll need to grab a portable shower or find campgrounds with amenities.
Now, if we take all this and place ourselves in the middle, we have can tap into an experience that may not be ready for prolonged off-grid use, but the few days we can spend out there will still be filled with mornings where the only sounds you hear are the leaves rustling in the trees or a brook babbling about nearby.
From here, you lean over to your significant other, give them a kiss on the cheek, and then climb out of bed, open the rear door, step out into the toilet annex you added outside, and do your bidding. After, wash those hands and put a pot of coffee on the gas top you brought along.
Photo: Micro Camper Since the smell of roasted coffee has also lifted your significant other from his or her slumber, something your magical kiss couldn’t do, you both head back outside where you plop down on a couple of chairs to take in the sights and sounds of today’s morning. Stay there for a bit, but don’t forget about breakfast; you have some bike riding, kayaking, or fishing to do today.
The rest is up to your imagination, but there is a bit of room for improvement, if you ask me. What I can see lacking here is a more equipped electrical system, but this can easily be resolved with a portable power bank and some solar panels, and these days, there are plenty to choose from. EcoFlow and Jackery are some very often-called-upon brands with a great reputation.
Considering that you will have plenty pf cash left over after your Midi Cargo XL acquisition, you should be fine. I mean with some dealers selling a Full version for as low as €8,500 (without local taxes) is quite the deal. That’s the equivalent to $9,500, marking it as one of the most inexpensive toy hauler campers I've covered this year.
The downside to Tomplan goodies, at least, pertaining to North Americans, is that this brand doesn’t sell in the US. If you do want to get your hands on one, you’ll need to cover shipping and import fees, not to mention modifications to make it road legal in the US, if it’s not.
